findings.title: Repo identity is the bare repo name, so two discovered repos with the same name merge silently
findings.claim: Node IDs are namespaced by "the repo name". Discovery now finds repos two levels down, explicitly to support `~/src/<org>/<repo>` trees. Nothing in the architecture or contracts says what happens when two discovered repos share a name (a fork and its upstream, `team-a/api` and `team-b/api`, a submodule named like a sibling). The fact-merging rule then joins their nodes: evidence is unioned and scalars go to the higher tier. A person's override on one repo also applies to the other. The map is wrong and nothing says so.
findings.evidence: architecture.md "IDs and aliases": "The namespace is the repo name"; "Merging facts. When two extractors emit the same node ID, evidence unions and scalar fields take the more specific tier's value". DR-71 Context names the `~/src/<org>/<repo>` layout as a target, and its Decision adds "repos two levels down when the first level has none". contracts.md defines NodeId only as "<namespace>:<kind-short>:<key>", with no uniqueness rule, error code or warning for a duplicate namespace. This conflicts with KICKOFF R1 ("every higher level is a faithful roll-up") and principle 1 ("Never lose or overwrite what someone did").
findings.failure_scenario: The user opens Claude Code in `~/src`, which holds `me/planroom` (a fork) and `upstream/planroom`. `scan` finds both as `planroom`. `planroom:dir:src/x` is now one node with evidence from both trees. `ask path` answers with hops from either repo, and a regroup the person makes "in the fork" also moves the upstream's directory. The reconciler sees a fact delta from whichever repo moved and may classify the other repo's commits against it. No error or warning appears.
findings.proposed_fix: Give each repo a unique namespace at discovery. Use the name when it's unique; otherwise use the shortest unique path suffix (`me-planroom`, `upstream-planroom`). Record the mapping from repo root to namespace in the store so it stays stable across scans. Add a `repo_name_collision` warning to the first scan summary, and a `first_run.rs::same_named_repos_get_distinct_namespaces` test. Document the rule in contracts.md next to NodeId.

findings.title: No ID continuity across engine upgrades, git renames or repo renames, so a person's corrections detach
findings.claim: Person edits target fact IDs: paths for nodes, and sha256(kind‖from‖to‖via) for edges. The design treats facts as freely recomputable across versions and has no ID-stability guarantee or test between releases. It has no rename detection either, and no rule for a repo that is renamed, moved or no longer discovered. When an upgrade changes how a built-in extractor keys a node or fills `via`, or a person runs `git mv` on a directory they regrouped, or renames a repo directory, every affected override becomes an orphan. Each one then goes to the person-stakes `override_retarget` card, which never auto-acts, even when git's own rename detection already gives the answer.
findings.evidence: architecture.md "Store schema": "Only `events` needs care across versions, because facts rebuild by rescanning". The migration tests cover only the DB schema ("ships with a fixture database from the previous release"). "The fold" step 5: "A target that vanished raises the decision bound to the `rescan.retarget` role." Decision kinds table: `override_retarget` ... "no" auto ... "person". A search for rename detection (`-M`, `find-renames`, `git mv`) and for repo removal or rename finds nothing. This conflicts with KICKOFF R6 ("Corrections survive every rescan") and principle 1 ("Never ask what a good default could answer").
findings.failure_scenario: The user upgrades from v0.1.0 to v0.1.1, where a linker fix changes the `via` of `orders -> redis`. The first rescan after the upgrade detaches the person's confirm on that edge and their `forbid` rule, so the intended-vs-actual diff silently loses a rule and the reconciler stops checking it. Separately, the person regrouped `storefront/src/cart` under `purchase` and later runs `git mv src/cart src/basket`. The regroup detaches, the map shows `basket` back under its old parent, and a card asks for a pick git already knows (100% similarity). If they rename the `worker` checkout to `worker-svc`, every override in that namespace detaches at once.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an ID-continuity layer. (1) A golden test, `id_stability.rs`, that compares the fixture's node and edge IDs with the previous release's committed list, plus an `id_aliases` migration table shipped with any release that changes an ID, which the fold applies before step 5. (2) In the git extractor, use `git diff -M --name-status -z` between the old and new snapshots so that a 100% rename becomes a deterministic retarget, recorded as an edit with `cause = scan` and undoable, with no card. Partial-similarity renames become the card's pre-selected candidate. (3) Key the repo namespace by a stable repo identity, such as its first commit or remote URL recorded at first scan, so a renamed or moved checkout keeps its namespace. A repo that is no longer discovered keeps its last snapshot, with a `repo_missing` warning, instead of orphaning its overrides.

findings.title: The temporary-host backup tells model-visible output to push private plan data to `origin`, with no privacy check
findings.claim: On a cloud session, Codespace or dev container, the backup of every person-authored event goes to `refs/planroom/backup/<id>` in "the root when it's a repo, else the first repo by name". The `temporary_host` warning carries the exact `git push origin 'refs/planroom/backup/*:...'` command in its `details`. Warnings travel in every envelope, so the chat model sees an imperative push instruction in tool output. The main thread is not barred from pushing (the guard blocks `git push` only for the implementer). Nothing checks or says whether that remote is public, or whether the chosen repo is the one the plan is about. Pushing publishes the plans, intents, breakdown text edits and decision history to anyone who can read that remote.
findings.evidence: architecture.md "Store schema" > "Temporary hosts": "commits the backup file to `refs/planroom/backup/<workspace_id>` in one workspace repo: the root when it's a repo, else the first repo by name ... To keep them, run git push origin 'refs/planroom/backup/*:refs/planroom/backup/*'." contracts.md warning `temporary_host`: "`details {repo, ref, push}`, the exact push command". The guard rule "denies its `sqlite3`, `script`, `git push` and `planroom handoff`" applies to the implementer only (DR-52/DR-64). The Security table has no row for the backup ref leaving the machine. This conflicts with the KICKOFF security bar and the design's own "What leaves the machine" consent principle, which covers model calls but not this path.
findings.failure_scenario: The user works in a Claude Code cloud session (KICKOFF's own environment) on a workspace whose first repo by name is a public OSS repo. The status line and the `focus` tool result say "To keep them, run git push origin ...". In auto mode the chat model, trying to be helpful, runs the push. The private roadmap ("Add retries to the worker", pre-mortem notes, rejected options, breakdown edits of internal prompts) is now fetchable from the public GitHub repo. A person following the line by hand does the same without knowing the ref is public.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat the push as a person-only, consented step, not advice. Remove the command from model-visible `details` (keep `{repo, ref}` only). Show the push as a pane or band press that runs it with a person token, after a one-line card naming the remote URL and whether its host reports it public: "Push your Planroom backup (214 edits, plan text) to github.com/acme/orders? Anyone who can read that repo can read it." Let the person choose which repo holds the ref, defaulting to a private one when one is known. Add a `tool.check` rule denying agent Bash `git push` of `refs/planroom/*`, a test `backup.rs::the_push_command_is_not_in_model_output`, and a SECURITY.md line.

findings.title: For a single-repo workspace the store sits in the working tree, where build contexts and copies pick it up
findings.claim: When the workspace is a single repo, `.planroom/` (store.db with every event, plan text, model_cache responses, the Artifact `pairing_key` HMAC secret and `serve.json`'s control token) lives in the repo's working tree. It is protected only by a nested `.gitignore` of `*`. Docker build contexts, `rsync`/`scp -r`, zip uploads and many deploy tools ignore `.gitignore`, so a `COPY . .` bakes the store into an image that may be pushed to a registry. The design already moves the store to the data root for unsafe filesystems, but not for this case. The fixture's workspace root is a parent directory, so this layout is never exercised.
findings.evidence: architecture.md "Where the workspace lives": "The repos are the root itself if it's a git repo"; "`.planroom/` holds `store.db` ..., `serve.json` (port, pid, version, catalogue hash, control token), ... and a `.gitignore` of `*`". The `meta` table holds `pairing_key [DR-67]`. DR-72: "a leaked store lets someone forge only Artifact inbox rows", so the design treats a leaked store as a real threat. A search for `.dockerignore`/build context finds nothing. Fixture: `OUT/{storefront,orders,worker,kit,platform}` puts `.planroom/` outside every repo. Conflicts with KICKOFF R15 (Iris security bar) and the brief's security criterion.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs Planroom in their single service repo whose Dockerfile does `COPY . /app`, and CI runs `docker build . && docker push ghcr.io/acme/svc` (public). The image now contains `/app/.planroom/store.db` with the full plan history, decision records, cached model responses over repo excerpts, and the pairing key. With the key, anyone who can also write as the owner to the Artifact `db` can forge signed phone rows, and the plan content is public.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep `store.db` and its WAL under `DATA_ROOT/stores/<workspace_id>/` for every workspace, and leave only `store.pointer`, a non-secret `config.toml` and the `.gitignore` in `.planroom/`. Move `serve.json`'s control token to the data root as well. The pointer mechanism already exists for unsafe filesystems, so this is a default change, not a new mechanism. Add a test `fs_check.rs::a_single_repo_workspace_keeps_no_secret_in_the_tree`, and run S1 once on a single-repo workspace.

findings.title: The mod targets an early-access host API pinned only in CI, with no runtime compatibility check or degradation
findings.claim: The mod API "may change between releases without notice". The design pins Claude Code 2.1.310 only inside `xtask` and CI (auto-update off), while every user, including the owner at release time, runs an auto-updating Claude Code. The mod's start-up checks the engine's version and catalogue hash, but never the host's API surface. No supported Claude Code range is declared, and no CI job runs `claude plugin test` against the latest release. If a `$` API moves, the pane, band, `/room` and every press (all person-only actions: card picks, `handoff start`/`merge`, `open`) break, with no fallback pane explaining why.
findings.evidence: research/mod-api.md §10.1: "Early access. The API 'may change between releases without notice' [T:4]. Pin Claude Code 2.1.310 in CI". repo-layout.md toolchain table: "Claude Code 2.1.310 | an `xtask` constant; `xtask` installs that exact version with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`". `toolchain.yml` does only "weekly pin-age checks". architecture.md "Wiring" steps 1 to 5 detect a Windows host, a missing engine and a version mismatch, but never the host version or API shape. The fallback-pane list has no host-incompatibility state. KICKOFF S14 runs the install "in a fresh session" on the owner's live Claude Code; S9 drives every flow from the mod; principle 1: "Never show a blank state."
findings.failure_scenario: Claude Code auto-updates to 2.1.33x between the build and the owner's release check, and renames a field `session.start` reads, or changes a `ui` node type. The mod throws during registration: no pane, no `/room`, no tools. S14 step 3 and S9 fail in the owner's live session, and a public user sees nothing, with no message pointing to the skills-only path. CI stays green because it pins 2.1.310.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) In `session.start`, before registering anything, feature-detect each `$` member the mod uses, and wrap registration in try/catch. On a mismatch, register only the `/room` command (or nothing) and show a status line from `en.toml`: "This Claude Code (2.1.33x) changed the mod API Planroom 0.1 uses; skills still work. Update Planroom." Add an `unsupported_host` fallback pane. (2) Add a scheduled, non-gating `host-canary.yml` job that installs the latest Claude Code, runs `claude plugin test target/mod-test` and the install script, and opens an issue on failure. (3) Have `doctor` report the host version, and document the tested range in plugin/README.md.

findings.title: Hand-off results can only land by a local merge into main; a PR or squash-merge never closes the loop
findings.claim: The only way a hand-off reaches a repo is the person-only `handoff merge`, which runs `git merge --no-ff planroom/KEY` into the local tracked branch. For repos on GitHub with branch protection or a PR-and-squash workflow, the usual flow is to push `planroom/KEY`, open a PR, squash or rebase-merge it, and pull. The design doesn't define that path. A local merge commit can't be pushed to a protected main. When the work lands through a squash, `planroom/KEY` is never an ancestor and the hand-off stays `reviewing`. The item stays "in progress (unmerged hand-off branch)", and the squash commit touches the item's touch points, so it can't be placed and raises a residual card.
findings.evidence: architecture.md "The hand-off loop": `reviewing --> merging: person merges after the preflight` is the only route to `merged`. "The reconciler" rule 2: "whose hand-off branches are merged is `done`" (how "merged" is determined is unspecified). Rule 3: "an unmerged hand-off branch" is in progress. Rule 5 excludes units "touching an in-progress item's `kernel.touches` targets" from unplanned, and rule 6 sends what can't be placed to `reconcile.residual`'s card. A search for squash, pull request or a merged-outside-Planroom path finds nothing. This conflicts with KICKOFF R8 ("reconciliation closes the loop after merge") and principle 1 (interrupt only for decisions only the person can make).
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's repos are on GitHub with protected `main`. After S4-style review, they push `planroom/worker-status-via-api` and squash-merge the PR on GitHub, then `git pull`. Planroom still shows the hand-off as reviewing and the item in progress. The next scan deals a residual card for the squash commit. If they press merge instead, the local merge commit is rejected by `git push`, and undoing it (`handoff revert`, or a reset that reads as "rewritten") restarts reconciliation with nothing classified.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a second landing path. On the review card, offer "Push branch for a PR" (person-only; pushes `planroom/KEY` and prints the compare URL), and add a `merged_externally` transition. A scan marks a hand-off merged when the tracked branch gains a commit whose `git patch-id --stable` matches the branch's combined diff, or whose tree contains the branch's changes and whose message names KEY. That commit becomes a hand-off unit, not a residual. Add tests `reconcile.rs::a_squash_merged_handoff_is_done` and `a_rebase_merged_handoff_is_done`.

findings.title: If the canvas port moves, the tab's unsent edits are stranded in the old origin's localStorage
findings.claim: Unsent canvas edits live in `localStorage`, which the browser scopes to origin (scheme, host and port). `serve` reuses the recorded port but takes a free one "only when that one is taken". After a port move, the new login link opens a new origin, which can't see the old origin's pending edits. The old tab can't reach the new server either. Nothing reserves a port per workspace across workspaces, so another workspace's `serve` or any local program can take the recorded port while this one is down. The edits are counted on the old tab but can never be flushed.
findings.evidence: architecture.md "The canvas" > Writes: "Pending edits live in `localStorage`, keyed by workspace ID ... Any signed-in tab of that workspace flushes them". "Local server and live stream": "binds `127.0.0.1` on the port its workspace's last `serve.json` recorded, and on a free port only when that one is taken ... A stable port keeps the canvas's origin, and with it the tab's storage". "Auth": a tab without a token shows "This tab needs a fresh link: press e in the pane", with its pending edits counted. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 1 ("Never lose ... what someone did") and R10 ("No write is lost").
findings.failure_scenario: The engine dies or the laptop reboots while the person keeps editing in the open tab, so three regroups queue in localStorage under 127.0.0.1:41873. After the reboot, a second workspace's `serve` (or a dev server) starts first and takes 41873. The first workspace's `serve` moves to 41902. The person presses `e`, signs in on the new origin, and sees none of the three edits. The old tab shows "3 pending" but can never deliver them. Likelihood is low, but the loss is silent.
findings.proposed_fix: Assign each workspace a port in `DATA_ROOT/workspaces.json` that no other workspace may record, so Planroom never collides with itself. If the recorded port is held by another program, have `open` say so in one line and offer to retry, rather than moving silently. As a backstop, have a tab that holds pending edits and can't sign in offer "Save 3 unsent edits", which downloads a `planroom.inbox/v1` file the person can bring in with the person-only `import`. Add an e2e test, `edits_survive_a_port_move`.

findings.title: The git 2.35.2 minimum turns away Ubuntu 22.04's default git, and what the user sees is undefined
findings.claim: Git 2.35.2 or later is required so that `safe.directory` refuses a repo another user owns. The minimum is enforced only in `doctor`, and the scan-time behavior below it is undefined. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, still a common WSL 2 and server distro, ships git 2.34.1 with the safe.directory fix backported, so a version-string check rejects a safe git. Debian 11 ships 2.30.2. Either the engine refuses to scan on those hosts with no defined message, or it runs and the ownership protection it relies on is silently absent on a genuinely unpatched git. CI runs ubuntu-24.04 and macOS only, so neither case is tested.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Adapters table: "the `git` CLI, at least 2.35.2, which refuses a repo another user owns". Risks R-11: "a minimum version of 2.35.2 in `doctor`". repo-layout.md: "git 2.35.2 or later [DR-64] | `planroom doctor`, CI setup". contracts.md has no `git_too_old` or similar code. Ubuntu jammy's git package is 1:2.34.1-1ubuntu1.x (not verified in this container).
findings.failure_scenario: A user on WSL 2 with Ubuntu-22.04 installs the plugin. The first `scan` either fails with a generic error, leaving the pane on `failed` with no fix line, or proceeds without the ownership guarantee the security table promises.
findings.proposed_fix: Check repository ownership in the engine (`stat` the repo's `.git` and compare its owner with `geteuid`), so the guarantee doesn't depend on git's version. Lower the hard minimum to the oldest git whose plumbing flags the adapter uses (check this in WS3). Add a stable error code with a one-line fix for git below that floor, and a CI job in an ubuntu:22.04 container.

findings.title: Store and backup growth has no bound: events, blob_facts, model_cache and events.ndjson are never pruned
findings.claim: Only snapshots are pruned (the last 20 per repo). Every rescan appends a `scan` event, and decisions, claims and hand-off steps append events forever. Each commit's changed blobs add `blob_facts` rows, and every `packs_hash` change (every engine upgrade) duplicates the cache. `model_cache` keeps every response, and `events.ndjson` is append-only. The fold is computed on read over all events on every command, but its budget is set at 5,000 events, which a few months of commit-triggered rescans across 5 repos will pass. Each `VACUUM INTO` migration copy is a full-size store.
findings.evidence: architecture.md "Versions and revisions": "pruned after the last 20 per repo" (snapshots only). "Store schema": no retention for `blob_facts`, `model_cache` or the backup file. "Performance budgets": "Fold under 50 ms at 20,000 facts and 5,000 events". R-2 and bet 2 name a fold cache only as a fallback. DR-47 lists "a generated large-repo test" as a known gap.
findings.failure_scenario: After six months of daily use with agents committing often, the store holds about 60,000 events and several stale `packs_hash` generations of blob facts. Every `focus` refresh folds every event. The pane and canvas drift past the 1 s live bar, and the three pre-migration copies take a large amount of disk.
findings.proposed_fix: Add retention for derived and cached tables: `blob_facts` and `model_cache` rows whose `packs_hash` or model is not current, or which no snapshot within the last 20 per repo references, are deleted by a `gc` duty under a lease. Rotate `events.ndjson` once per store version. Add a fold benchmark at 50,000 events to `budgets.json` as evidence, and state the growth model in the Performance section.

findings.title: "Remove Planroom" claims to list everything Planroom creates but omits the published Artifact and paired devices
findings.claim: The removal guide lists the local artifacts (serve, `.planroom/`, the data root, refs, config, the plugin) and says it lists "everything Planroom creates". It leaves out the Artifact page published on claude.ai, which holds the redacted map snapshot, plan text and the `db` (`live/head`, inbox rows and acks, including other viewers' rows), and the pairing key each paired phone keeps in `localStorage`. There is also no command or skill path to stop sharing or unpublish. After uninstall, the remote copy of the map and plans stays available to anyone it was shared with.
findings.evidence: architecture.md "Packaging and release": "The guides include 'Remove Planroom', which lists everything Planroom creates, in the order to remove it: a detached `serve`, each workspace's `.planroom/`, the data root, `planroom/*` branches, `refs/planroom/archive/*` and `refs/planroom/backup/*`, the user-level config directory ... and the plugin itself". "Remote mode" step 8: the page "keeps [the pairing key] in its `localStorage`". A search for unpublish or stop-sharing finds nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner shared the Artifact with a colleague for S11, later uninstalls Planroom following the guide, and believes nothing remains. The colleague can still open the snapshot of the workspace map and plan.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the Artifact to the removal guide, and add a `/room share --stop` path. It returns the exact Artifact `delete` arguments for the chat model to run after a person's press, and clears `meta.pairing_key`. Add a `docs.rs` test that the guide's list matches every location the contracts name, the Artifact URL included.

verdicts.reason: The namespace is the bare repo name. Discovery now reaches grandchildren, and same-ID facts merge. Nothing in the docs keeps two same-named repos apart or warns about them, so the silent merge in the failure scenario can happen. It corrupts the R1 roll-up and lets one repo's override apply to the other, so it is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:305 "The namespace is the repo name"; architecture.md:509 "its grandchildren that are" [DR-71]; decisions.md:770 "When two extractors emit the same node ID, evidence unions and scalar fields take the more specific tier's value." contracts.md:343 defines NodeId with no uniqueness rule. A grep for collision, duplicate, same-name or unique repo handling finds nothing.

verdicts.reason: The finding overstates one thing: a vanished target is not silent. It raises the `rescan.retarget` card and is listed in Diffs (architecture.md:368, 881). The core gap is still real. The docs have no rename detection, no ID-stability test across releases and no stable repo identity. So a `git mv` that git already resolves at 100% detaches the regroup, which the person-stakes card's default leaves detached, and the person has to pick by hand. That breaks principle 1 ("Never ask what a good default could answer"). A repo directory rename orphans every override in that namespace.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:368 "A target that vanished raises the decision bound to the `rescan.retarget` role"; architecture.md:881 `override_retarget`: auto "no", stakes "person", default "keep the override detached, listed in Diffs". architecture.md:497 "Only `events` needs care across versions, because facts rebuild by rescanning." Grep for find-renames, -M, git mv and id_stab: no hits.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: the `temporary_host` warning carries the exact push command in `details`, and tool results return `warnings` to the model. The guard denies `git push` only to the spawned implementer, not to the main thread. Nothing checks which remote, or how public it is, receives private plan history. This is a credible data-exposure risk, so it is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:503 "To keep them, run git push origin 'refs/planroom/backup/*:refs/planroom/backup/*'. Planroom never pushes it." contracts.md:205 `temporary_host` "details {repo, ref, push}, the exact push command". architecture.md:1279 (Wiring) tool results include `meta` `warnings`. architecture.md:406-408 puts the `git push` deny under "For a spawned planroom:implementer" only. The Security table row at architecture.md:1371 mentions the backup ref but no privacy check.

verdicts.reason: In a single-repo workspace, `.planroom/` sits in the working tree with store.db, `meta.pairing_key` and serve.json's control token, behind only a `.gitignore`. The store moves to DATA_ROOT only for unsafe filesystems. DR-53 itself acknowledges the store "sits inside the repo's working tree" and fixes only the `git clean` loss, not leaks through tools that ignore .gitignore (Docker build contexts, rsync). This is a real leak risk, so it is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:511 ".planroom/ holds store.db ..., serve.json (port, pid, version, catalogue hash, control token)... and a .gitignore of *"; architecture.md:512 moves the store only for network, WSL, FUSE and sync mounts; architecture.md:463 meta holds pairing_key [DR-67]; decisions.md:1016 "for a single-repo workspace sits inside the repo's working tree behind a .gitignore of *". Grep for dockerignore or build context: no hits.

verdicts.reason: Claude Code 2.1.310 is pinned only in xtask and CI. The mod start-up checks the engine's version and catalogue hash but never the host's version or API shape, and no fallback pane covers an unsupported host. The Risks table has no entry for the early-access mod API changing. A host auto-update could break S14 and S9 in the owner's live session while CI stays green.
verdicts.evidence: repo-layout.md:285 "Claude Code 2.1.310 | an xtask constant; xtask installs that exact version with DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1". The architecture.md Wiring steps (around line 1238) compare only the engine's version and catalogue hash. The fallback-pane list at architecture.md:1246 has fetching, build_offered, building, failed, unsupported_platform, version_mismatch, store_busy and person_key_mismatch, and no host-incompatibility state. Grep for "early access", "without notice" and host version in the architecture and decisions docs finds nothing.

verdicts.reason: The only route to `merged` is the local `handoff merge`. The reconciler counts a hand-off as done only when its branch is merged, and treats an unmerged branch as in progress. Rule 5 keeps a squash commit that touches an in-progress item's targets out of `unplanned`, so it falls through to the residual card. A squash or PR workflow therefore leaves the item stuck and deals a card the rules could have answered.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1080-1084 Rule 2 "whose hand-off branches are merged is done"; Rule 3 "an unmerged hand-off branch"; Rule 5 "not touching an in-progress item's kernel.touches targets"; Rule 6 "raises the reconcile.residual role's card". Grep for squash, patch-id and merged-externally: no hits.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: pending edits live in origin-scoped `localStorage`, and `serve` moves to a free port when its recorded one is taken. The design's own argument that the edits survive depends on the origin staying stable. No per-workspace port reservation, and no export path for a stranded tab, exists. The case is unlikely, but it silently loses a person's edits, which counts as material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1208 "on a free port only when that one is taken ... A stable port keeps the canvas's origin, and with it the tab's storage"; architecture.md:1309 "Pending edits live in localStorage, keyed by workspace ID". `workspaces.json` maps only root to workspace_id (architecture.md:513).

verdicts.reason: Real, and correctly rated minor. The 2.35.2 floor is enforced only in `doctor`, no error code exists for an older git, and CI covers only ubuntu-24.04 and macOS. Ubuntu 22.04's backported 2.34.1 is likely to be misjudged by a version-string check (I did not verify this here).
